correctness.rationale: Euler gives F=Σx_i∂_iF in characteristic two. No projective gradient zero means height four; the four homogeneous quadrics are then a regular sequence in the polynomial ring and the quotient has Hilbert series (1+t)^4. Conversely, full quintic image includes each x_i^5, which rules out any projective gradient zero. Thus the rank-56 test is geometric and works over the base field. With a separately written column-elimination implementation and variable swaps plus a shear generating GL4(F2), I regenerated all 141 nonzero-form orbits, the 36 smooth orbits and 322,560 smooth forms. The regenerated smooth bitmap and the representative/size keys agree exactly with the packaged data. For every orbit representative F I counted compatible G and used 15−popcount of the union of their nonzero-point masks; the weighted bins divide by six because F,G,F+G are the three nonzero forms and every pencil has six ordered bases. All 16 bins matched, totaling 5,002,905,600. A separate Walsh evaluation on the regenerated indicator yielded 30,017,433,600 ordered triples. Parity of cubic evaluations follows monomial by monomial since each leaves an unused variable; this independently excludes exactly fourteen common points. For fifteen points the Boolean reductions leave precisely the alternating pair terms, and the gradient is A times the coordinate-wise squares. I independently found 28 such smooth forms and 56 compatible pencils, one orbit with stabilizer 360. For each extremal pencil I checked the middle coefficients of each member's binary cubic restriction on all 35 rational lines; endpoints vanish already. The five contained lines in every case give each rational point exactly once, so they are pairwise skew.
residual_risks: The Groebner and C++ programs are recorded corroboration, not a second live replay here. The independently regenerated census relies on the proved quintic-rank criterion. No assertion is made about the complete intersection scheme beyond the rational point and line statements.

value.rationale: Lines wholly in the smooth parameter set are a natural exact finite instance of the finite-field smooth pencil problem. The rational common zero set is invariant under both coordinate changes and choice of basis and is a natural way to refine a total. The histogram quantifies the full spectrum rather than recomputing a known surface table: in particular the top two bins distinguish an impossible size from an attained extremal size with a skew-line spread and one symmetry type. This is usable benchmark data for additive incidence in smooth cubic forms.
residual_risks: The result is for one natural small field and degree and is not a formula for other fields or a classification of all pencil symmetry types.
